experiment_contract.claim: Test whether averaging multiple deterministic replicas of the exact current LambdaRank trainer improves portfolio contribution versus a single replica.
experiment_contract.expected_observable: meta/training artifact reflects multiple fitted models and prediction differs from single-model parent on the same split/seed
experiment_contract.falsification_condition: No positive paired delta versus parent or evidence that averaged predictions collapse to the single-model ordering.

required_components: train block must call SO.train at least 3 times with distinct deterministic seeds
predict block must average all stored model predictions
predict block jitter must depend on both user_id and video_id and remain tiny

proposal.fallback: Remove jitter first and keep pure averaging if audit/runtime is tight; if cost is prohibitive, reduce to 2 replicas.
proposal.hypothesis: A small within-mechanism ensemble of the current LambdaRank model will reduce variance and produce rank orders complementary to the active portfolio, improving marginal portfolio primary even if standalone gain is small.
proposal.implementation_plan: Patch train and predict. In train, keep SO.train exact config/grouping but train 3 LightGBM rankers per seed using deterministic sub-seeds {seed, seed+101, seed+202} and the same Xs/y, storing the list in one model object. In predict, average member predictions and add a tiny deterministic inference-time tab-conditioned score jitter based on hashed (user_id, video_id) scaled to ~1e-6 only to break ties differently across users/items without changing coarse score structure. No feature or target changes.
proposal.justification: For a diverse but weaker branch, averaging nearby stochastic rankers often preserves mechanism identity while smoothing idiosyncratic errors. Because portfolio search reward is marginal contribution, a modestly smoother but still distinct LambdaRank member is a plausible refinement. The tiny deterministic jitter only resolves ties at the user-item level, which can matter for nDCG@5 and cannot be achieved by a per-user constant.
proposal.observation: The selected parent is "item_lambdarank" with standalone_primary 0.6010575837714116, while portfolio diagnostics show lower within-user rank correlation versus the other members (0.8224356227038319 and 0.8327371603950816), indicating this branch already contributes diversity; current code trains exactly one SO.train model per seed.

research_evidence.query: Can the validated heterogeneous portfolio use a fixed label-free context router without weakening the test firewall?
research_evidence.reason: The global 0.4/0.4/0.2 mixture leaves stable tab-specific member specialization unused, while fitting a flexible gate would add excessive validation degrees of freedom.
research_evidence.summary: Pre-register the five coarse tab routes over the locked Legal, DeepFM engagement MTL, and item LambdaRank members. Keep 0.4/0.4/0.2 as fallback and route only tabs with at least 1,000 official-validation rows on a 0.1 weight grid. The global portfolio scored 0.605828080 and the fixed router scored 0.606127749. All matched seeds improved by [+0.000242107,+0.000150108,+0.000211008], mean +0.000201074, clearing the predeclared all-seed mean >=0.00015 gate although the paired-user CI crossed zero. The formal run must translate stable operator IDs to fresh node IDs, reproduce the exact score and seed deltas before LLM search, never refit routes during warm-start, and use only inference-time tab on test.

matches.hypothesis: A censored watch-time auxiliary objective will shape embeddings toward fine-grained dwell preference complementary to binary long_view, yielding better within-user ordering and potentially more error diversity relative to the current portfolio.
matches.implementation_plan: Edit target, model, and train blocks. Keep long_view as the main objective. In target, derive a train-only watch-time target from DV.watch_ratio() and RowSet.duration_ms: compute valid rows from the returned mask, transform observed play ratio and duration with a bounded log-scale target such as log1p(ratio * duration_ms)/12 and log1p(duration_ms)/12. In model/train, add one scalar auxiliary regression head sharing the existing representation with the main multitask tower. For rows flagged complete by watch_ratio validity and ratio near/full completion, use a one-sided lower-bound hinge against log-duration; for incomplete valid rows use squared error or smooth L1 to the transformed watch-time target. Combine this with the existing long_view plus engagement auxiliary objective using a small fixed weight (for example retain aux_weight 0.2 for existing heads and add a separate small watch loss weight implemented visibly in train). No watch-time values may be used as inference features.
matches.mechanism: censored watch-time auxiliary head for long_view

proposal.hypothesis: The parent LambdaRank branch has tab-structured score miscalibration; a fixed tab-conditional monotone transform can improve top-5 ordering and diversify against the other members without retraining.
proposal.implementation_plan: Patch predict only. After SO.predict, load split rows via DV.load(split), and apply a fixed monotone piecewise-linear transform per coarse tab bucket {0,1,2,4,6,other}. Use predeclared slopes/intercepts centered near identity, with stronger expansion/compression only for tabs where the LambdaRank branch is diagnostically weak in the portfolio. The transform must be monotone within each tab so it changes cross-tab score comparability but preserves within-tab local ordering except for scale shifts; because users can see mixed tabs, this can alter within-user ranking legally using inference-time tab.
proposal.justification: Because both official metrics rank within user, any lawful context that varies by candidate can be used at prediction time. Tab is an exposed candidate/context field and diagnostics indicate systematic tab-specific weakness, making post-score calibration a targeted structural diversification hypothesis rather than scalar retuning.
proposal.mechanism: tab-specific monotone score calibration on LambdaRank outputs
proposal.observation: Portfolio diagnostics for w003 show strong tab disadvantages: delta_primary -0.01749022029153391 on tab=0 and -0.009346696620826433 on tab=2; the latest candidate also degraded tabs 0/1/2/6. The predict API explicitly allows calling DV.load(split) to read inference-time tab.
proposal.research_nonuse_reason: No supplied E### directly studies a fixed tab-specific monotone postscore transform for this single LambdaRank branch. The more direct basis is the exact tab-slice diagnostics plus the legal prediction-time access to tab in the runtime contract.

train block must fit both the unchanged SO.train LambdaRank model and an auxiliary regressor consuming Xs[train] on valid watch-ratio rows

proposal.hypothesis: A train-only watch-ratio auxiliary model fused at prediction time supplies complementary engagement structure aligned with long_view, improving within-user top-k ordering beyond pure LambdaRank.
proposal.implementation_plan: Patch target, train, and predict. Keep main trained ranker as the existing SO.train LambdaRank long_view model. In target, read DV.watch_ratio() on train only and construct a valid-mask plus clipped log1p watch-ratio target for train rows. In train, fit a lightweight secondary sklearn regressor on the same training rows and current Xs[train] to predict the auxiliary target only where valid is true; store both the LambdaRank model and auxiliary regressor. In predict, output base LambdaRank score plus a small fixed-weight auxiliary score contribution from the regressor, with no use of any post-exposure feature at inference because Xs are still the same legal inference-time features.
proposal.justification: This is a cross-branch mechanism fusion: w003 contributes a strong item/context ranker, while w002 demonstrates engagement modeling value in the portfolio. Adding a train-only continuous engagement auxiliary model preserves legal inference and may create a more complementary ordering, especially near the top of each user's slate.
proposal.mechanism: LambdaRank plus train-only censored watch-ratio auxiliary score fusion
proposal.observation: Research evidence reports that keeping native long_view as the ranking objective while adding a small censored watch-time head improved validation over BPR alone; deterministic diagnostics show train_target_phi_with_long_view for is_click is 0.7604858188163154 but other native actions are weaker, suggesting watch-depth can add a different continuous signal. The current parent uses only pointwise long_view target through SO.build_target.

research_evidence.query: How should watch time complement native long_view without changing evaluation labels?
research_evidence.reason: The native binary label discards engagement magnitude and completed plays are right-censored by duration.
research_evidence.summary: Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings. Transform play time and duration with log1p/12. For incomplete plays use exact regression residual; for completed plays use a one-sided lower-bound hinge that stops penalizing predictions above log-duration. Never use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone; on three random-exposure seeds, unbiased primary was 0.376328528 ± 0.003245064 versus 0.373291085 ± 0.002151737. This is an implementation prior, not permission to replace the fixed relevance label.

In build_features, after calling SO.build_features(splits, train_idx, OP_CONFIG), load DV.load('train') and compute train-only count dictionaries for user-author, user-video, and user-tab interactions over the training rows referenced by train_idx. For each split, append dense float32 columns: log1p(user_author_count), log1p(user_video_count), log1p(user_tab_count), and normalized user_author_share = user_author_count / max(1,user_total_count). Counts use only train data; unseen pairs map to zero. In predict, keep SO.predict unchanged because the model consumes the expanded matrices directly.

rejected: A small within-mechanism ensemble of the current LambdaRank model will reduce variance and produce rank orders complementary to the active portfolio, improving marginal portfolio primary even if standalone gain is small.
A train-only watch-ratio auxiliary model fused at prediction time supplies complementary engagement structure aligned with long_view, improving within-user top-k ordering beyond pure LambdaRank.
selection_rationale: Candidate 0 is executable and portfolio-aligned because w003 is already the most diverse member, but its evidence is indirect: E002 supports label-free combination of heterogeneous validated rankers, not same-mechanism seed bagging, and the tiny tie-jitter is likely inert unless many exact ties occur. It also has the highest cost and a meaningful risk that averaging nearby LambdaRank replicas reduces the very diversity that makes w003 useful marginally, so expected marginal portfolio gain times reliability is only moderate despite good code connectivity. Candidate 1 is the strongest next experiment because it is directly connected to an executable prediction consumer, uses legal inference-time tab context, targets a concrete diagnosed weakness of w003 on tabs 0 and 2, satisfies the requirement to include a structural residual-targeted/error-diverse idea, and is cheap and highly falsifiable. Although it lacks external research support, its evidence is the most dataset-specific and the implementation is simple enough that measured outcome will be attributable to the hypothesis rather than plumbing risk. Candidate 2 is also connected and offers a true mechanism-fusion path, but its supporting research is only a translated mechanism from a different model family, the implementation spans target/train/predict with more opportunities for mismatch, and late fusion of a censored auxiliary regressor is less reliable than the direct tab-diagnostic correction in Candidate 1. Therefore Candidate 1 has the best expected marginal portfolio primary gain after accounting for evidential reliability, implementation reliability, cost, and risk.
